- Mission: Managing a 28-Sol Artemis lunar base life support system at Shackleton Crater, Lunar South Pole (89.9°S).

- Critical Architecture: NASA ISS-standard closed-loop Sabatier and OGA electrolysis stoichiometry, +120°C / -180°C thermal cycle management, live NASA DONKI API solar storm integration, and multi-layered radiation shielding (HDPE + regolith + water wall).

- Innovative Features: Crew psychology/stress-dependent metabolic load adjustments, DRONE-01 3D digital twin patching hull breaches, and a 6-screen physical hardware command console CAD design.

- Education: Gemini 3.8 Flash-powered CAPCOM AI assistant and printable NASA flight certification for ages 7–12.

- Live Simulation Portal: https://frolicking-salamander-ad741a.netlify.app/

PROJECT DEEP-DIVE: APEX-ECLSS v11.0 OMNI-COMMAND

Team NUMERO 1078 (Aselsan MTAL, Ankara) | NASA Space Apps Challenge Ankara 2026

1. MISSION OVERVIEW & OBJECTIVES

- Target Location: Shackleton Crater, Lunar South Pole (89.9°S), operating under extreme thermal swings from +120°C in sunlight to -180°C in cryogenic darkness.

- Mission Duration: 28 Sols of continuous closed-loop Artemis base life support management.

- Core Challenge: Balancing competing engineering constraints—such as life support, radiation shielding, power budgets, and food production—without oversimplifying real mission trade-offs or overwhelming young learners.

2. SUB-SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE & PHYSICS

- Closed-Loop Stoichiometry (ECLSS): Modeled after NASA International Space Station (ISS) flight data. The Sabatier reactor captures crew-generated CO₂ and combines it with hydrogen to produce water and methane, while the Oxygen Generation Assembly (OGA) electrolysis unit splits water to replenish pure O₂.

- Thermal Control (ATCS): Regulates internal cabin temperatures against harsh external environments using variable cooling loops and nuclear waste heat recycling during lunar nights.

- Power Management: Combines deployable ROSA solar arrays, Li-S energy storage batteries, a methane fuel cell, and an optional NASA Kilopower fission reactor (10 kWe base load) to survive the 14-day night.

- Space Weather & Radiation Defense: Integrates live/archive NASA DONKI API solar flare (FLR) and CME data. Protects astronauts using High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) shielding, autonomous regolith sintering rovers, and an emergency water-walled storm shelter (+45% attenuation).

3. INNOVATIVE FEATURES & DIGITAL TWIN

- Human Factors & Crew Psychology: Simulates crew stress and morale. High stress or system failures increase metabolic O₂ demand by 20%, creating cascading mission risks.

- 3D Digital Twin & Drone Repair: An interactive isometric lunar base simulation where players deploy "DRONE-01" to patch structural micrometeorite hull breaches in real time.

- Physical Hardware Co-Design: Built in tandem with the "NUMERO 1078" physical 6-screen command console CAD design—featuring analog faders, a macro button matrix, an analog joystick, and an industrial emergency E-STOP button linked via USB-HID.

4. STEM EDUCATION (AGES 7–12)

- CAPCOM AI Co-Pilot: Powered by Gemini 3.8 Flash to provide instant engineering guidance and interactive Q&A for young space cadets.

- Artemis Flight Certification: Generates a customized, printable NASA mission diploma upon successful completion of the 28-Sol mission, tracking mass efficiency, recycling rates, and survival scores.

5. LIVE SIMULATION & RESOURCES

- Access the fully interactive web simulator at: https://frolicking-salamander-ad741a.netlify.app/
